note: Solana Labs, the San Francisco company that launched the Solana network (Wikipedia). The prefilled public status and $6.2M float are a match on an unrelated SEC filer (cik_weak), disputed: Solana Labs is private. Band on the SOL token network cap, $69.94B on CoinGecko on 2026-09-28, the basis a16z's row uses (no Solana Labs equity mark exists). Entry round not established: Solana Labs financed itself through SOL token sales, and the largest, the $314.15M private sale of June 2021 led by a16z and Polychain, does not name Ribbit (Solana's own announcement); Ribbit's archived Our Bets page lists Solana from August 2022. Stage undetermined; the record does not show how Ribbit bought in, so no token_funded flag.

Brazilian business bank headquartered in São Paulo (Bloomberg Línea). Ribbit led the $45M Series B of April 2022 after following the company since March 2020; the $13M Series A of December 2021 was led by Lachy Groom (Bloomberg Línea, 2022-04-11). Y Combinator's row carries San Francisco, US from its directory fields; this row records the São Paulo headquarters the press gives. Momentum check: no round at or above $1B found, news sweep 2026-09-28.

South African payments infrastructure company headquartered in Cape Town (Wikipedia). Ribbit led the $25M Series A extension of October 2023 (TechCrunch, 2023-10-02); the original $21M Series A of February 2022 was led by The Spruce House Partnership and TechCrunch's list of its investors does not name Ribbit. Ribbit took part in the $55M Series B of April 2025 as an existing funder (Wikipedia). Momentum check: no round at or above $1B found, news sweep 2026-09-28. The a16z, General Catalyst and Y Combinator rows named Stitch are other companies (Stitch Technologies, a US and London developer-tools startup): name collisions, not aligned.

note: São Paulo employee life-cycle and payroll platform (TechCrunch). Ribbit co-led the $13.2M seed with a16z (TechCrunch, 2024-11-11). An $18M round followed in July 2025, again led by Ribbit and a16z (LatamList), but the source gives it no round name and it is below twice the $13.2M seed, so it does not graduate the row; the entry is inside the 24-month window, so censored. a16z's row reads graduated on the $16M bar for an undisclosed seed amount, but LatamList and TechCrunch give $13.2M: raised for alignment. a16z's US country is an inferred value; this row cites São Paulo. Momentum check: no round at or above $1B found, news sweep 2026-09-28.

Mobile credit for emerging markets. 'Tala has raised more than $30 million in Series B financing, led by IVP and joined by Ribbit Capital', with Lowercase, Data Collective, Collaborative Fund and F3 named as the existing investors (the company's release, 2017-02-22), so Ribbit entered at the Series B. Ribbit was an existing investor in the $50M Series C of April 2018 (MediaNama), also held through its TL-C vehicle. The $145M Series E of October 2021 gave an enterprise valuation above $800M (Los Angeles Business Journal); no later round at or above $1B found, news sweep 2026-09-28. The prefilled Algeria (DZ) is a Wikidata namesake, disputed. City: Santa Monica (Los Angeles Business Journal, 2021); IVP's row carries Los Angeles, from the company's 2017 release.

Tax information reporting software for digital assets (Draper, Utah; aligned with the IVP and Insight rows). Ribbit's round is not on record: neither the $100M Series A of March 2021 (Paradigm and Tiger Global; PayPal's release lists the participants) nor the $130M Series B at $1.33B of August 2021 (IVP and Insight; the company's release) names Ribbit, and the firm's archive lists Taxbit from 2022. Stage undetermined. Mark: the Series B's $1.33B (company release, 2021-08-12), older than 24 months and aligned with the sibling rows; staff cuts and a CEO change in 2023 (Business Journals) carry no price.

Teya (SaltPay until 2023), payments and software for small merchants, London-based and incorporated in the Cayman Islands, backed by Tiger Global and Ribbit (City AM, 2026-02-03). No source read names Ribbit's round: SaltPay raised a $478M Series C in April 2021 with Tiger Global (UKTN), about $500M in 2021 by City AM's count, and Ribbit's archive lists SaltPay from 2022. Stage undetermined. Band aligned with Accel's row: UKTN (2022-05-18) gives SaltPay's valuation as $1bn after the 2021 Series C; the figure sits exactly on the $1B edge and is older than 24 months. Accel's cited Sifted page now returns 404.

Tomo (Tomo Networks, now Tomo Mortgage), digital mortgage lender founded by former Zillow executives. Ribbit co-led the $40M seed with Zigg Capital and NFX (GeekWire, 2020-10-27). Graduated: the $40M Series A of March 2022, led by SVB Capital with Ribbit participating, at a $640M valuation (GeekWire, 2022-03-21). Ribbit is also an existing investor in the $20M Series B of March 2025, when the company made New York its headquarters (GeekWire, 2025-03-11). The prefilled acquired status and Italy (IT) are a Wikidata namesake join, disputed: Tomo operates and is private. Last priced mark $640M (2022); no later round at or above $1B found, news sweep 2026-09-28. Bain Capital Ventures' Tomo (a personal AI coach, 2026) is another company; General Catalyst's 'Tomo, Inc.' is unresolved on that row.

Viva Republica, operator of the Toss super-app, Seoul (TechCrunch). 'In 2018, the company became a unicorn after raising $80 million in a funding round led by Kleiner Perkins and Ribbit Capital' (Wikipedia); the earlier backers Wikipedia names (Altos, PayPal, Sequoia China, GIC) do not include Ribbit, and Ribbit's January 2018 archived page does not list Toss. A late round at a $1.2B valuation reads Growth. Mark: the Series G of December 2022 at KRW 9.1 trillion (TechCrunch, 2022-12-19); KRW 9100.00B @ ECB 2022-12-19 (KRW/EUR 1377.17, EUR/USD 1.0598) = $7.00B, older than 24 months. Still private: the planned US listing was put on hold in July 2026 (Seoul Economic Daily).

Argentine digital bank based in Buenos Aires (the company's release). The $10M Series A announced 2018-02-06 was led by Soros Fund Management with Jefferies and Point72, and the company's release does not name Ribbit; Ribbit is named in the $34M Series B led by Goldman Sachs (LAVCA, 2018-10-03), its entry. Ribbit followed through its UA-D vehicle in the 2021 Series D. Mark: the $195M equity round led by Allianz X at $3.2B (Buenos Aires Times, 2026-03-04), up from $2.75B at the 2024 Series E.

Uniswap Labs, developer of the Uniswap protocol (New York; aligned with the a16z and USV rows). Ribbit's round is not on record: Uniswap's own Series A post (August 2020, $11M led by a16z) and the Series B coverage (TechCrunch and CoinDesk, October 2022, $165M led by Polychain) do not name Ribbit, and Ribbit's archive lists Uniswap from August 2022, before the Series B. Fortune's 2026 Crypto 100 entry for Ribbit names Uniswap as a holding without a round. Stage undetermined; the record does not show a token purchase either, so no token_funded flag. Mark: the Series B at $1.66B (TechCrunch, 2022-10-13), aligned with the sibling rows, older than 24 months; no equity round since.

Consumer credit and neobank, San Francisco (Wikipedia). USV's own post on the April 2017 round: 'We are excited to be Series A investors in this new venture, along with our friends at VY Capital, Sands Capital, FirstMark Capital, Ribbit Capital, Silicon Valley Bank and others'; the $60M Series A was Upgrade's first institutional round (Wikipedia), so Ribbit entered at the Series A. Ribbit followed through its UP-F vehicle in the November 2021 Series F and took part in the Series G as an existing shareholder (Wikipedia). Mark: the $165M Series G at $7.3B (Finovate, 2025-10-16), aligned with Coatue's row; USV's row carries the older $6.28B, same band. Private: an IPO is targeted, not filed.

AI-driven portfolio management for financial advisors, New York City (RIABiz). Ribbit led the $65M Series C of May 2021 (Institutional Investor; RIABiz has Sequoia and Ribbit), which matches the prefilled Growth entry from the 2021 Form D. Mark: the Series C 'based on a $1 billion valuation' (RIABiz, 2021-06-08), exactly on the $1B edge and older than 24 months; the 2023 reset (Business Insider) carries no priced round, so the mark stands. Aligned with Sequoia's row.

Vouch Insurance, business insurance for startups founded by Sam Hodges, San Francisco. Operating and private: it raised $25M in a round led by Ribbit in March 2024 (FinTech Global), and in August 2025 agreed to sell its MGA (Corix) and its carrier subsidiary to Hiscox USA, subject to regulatory approval, while Vouch continues as an independent broker (Coverager). No valuation at or above $1B found. First Round's 'Vouch' (a 2015 social-lending startup) is another company; Y Combinator's 'Vouch' (Summer 2019, Chicago) carries a defunct status copied from First Round's row, a possible misalignment if it is this company.

Warren Investimentos, Brazilian digital investment platform, headquartered in Porto Alegre (Portuguese Wikipedia). Ribbit led Warren's first institutional round, R$25M in March 2019 with Kaszek and Chromo Invest (LAVCA, 2019-03-28), which Wikipedia names the Series A; BRL 25.0M @ ECB 2019-03-28 (BRL/EUR 4.4592, EUR/USD 1.1218) = $6.3M. QED led the R$120M Series B (2020) and GIC the R$300M Series C (2021). Cocos Capital (Argentina) agreed in 2026 to buy Warren's brokerage (Warren Rena), asset management and capital markets operations, terms undisclosed, with closing subject to Brazilian regulatory approval (NeoFeed; Valor International, 2026-07-02); a signed, unclosed sale is not a status change, so the row stays private. No priced valuation at or above $1B found (the 'R$20 billion' figures are assets under custody).

Wave Mobile Money, mobile money across francophone West Africa, Senegal-based (TechCrunch, 2022). Its first priced round, the $200M Series A of September 2021 led by Sequoia Heritage and Founders Fund with Stripe and Ribbit, valued it at $1.7B (FinTech Global, 2021-09-07); Ribbit's archive lists Wave from 2022. The prefilled acquired status rides an SEC filer match on another Wave (cik_weak), disputed: the company operates (a EUR 117M debt facility in July 2025, TechAfrica News) and is private. The 2025 facility is debt, so the Series A mark stands, older than 24 months; aligned with Y Combinator's row. a16z's 'Wave' row is an unresolved different company.

Automated investing and cash management, Palo Alto (Wikipedia). Ribbit co-led the $35M round of April 2014 with Index Ventures (TechCrunch, 2014-04-02; Wikipedia adds Benchmark); TechCrunch names Social+Capital, Greylock and DAG as existing investors and Index as the 2013 round's lead, so this later round is Ribbit's entry and reads Growth (the source gives no series letter). Ribbit Capital II, L.P. appears among the investors in Wealthfront's 2025 registration statement (EDGAR full text). Public on Nasdaq since December 2025: the prefilled $0 float predates the listing, so the row is pinned by market cap, $1.56B on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis), same band as the Greylock and Spark rows.

Xapo Bank, a bitcoin-focused private bank headquartered in Gibraltar under a Gibraltar licence (Wikipedia); the headquarters moved from Palo Alto to Zug in 2015 and the institutional custody business went to Coinbase in 2019. Ribbit joined the $20M Series A of March 2014 led by Benchmark (Wikipedia), which matches the prefilled Series A from the Form D. Operating in 2026 (Crowdfund Insider, August 2026). No priced round at or above $1B found. Country: Gibraltar (GI) is missing from the pipeline's ISO table, so the row keeps the filing's US with city_country_conflict, as Greylock's row does; the correction is Erik's call.

Aave Labs (Aave Companies, then Avara), developer of the Aave lending protocol founded in 2017 as ETHLend (Wikipedia); its parent company is based in London (DL News, 2024-07-05), matching the firm's own 'United Kingdom' label on the archived Our Bets page (2022-2025). A member under the issuing organisation (decisions.md D2). No Aave financing read names Ribbit (Google News for Aave with Ribbit returns only Morpho items), so the entry round is undetermined, and the record does not show a token purchase, so no token_funded flag. Band on the AAVE token network cap, $2.28B on CoinGecko on 2026-09-28, the basis the a16z and Bain Capital Ventures books use for protocol rows with no equity mark (Solana, NEAR, Avalanche, World); no Aave Labs equity valuation was found.

AIUC (the Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company), insurance and a certification standard for AI agents, headquartered in San Francisco. Ribbit led the $40M Series A of September 2026 with First Harmonic (the company's release on Yahoo Finance, 2026-09-15); the $15M seed of July 2025 was led by Nat Friedman's NFDG and its investor list does not include Ribbit (Insurance Journal). Valuation undisclosed; momentum check: no round at or above $1B found, news sweep 2026-09-28.

Alpen Labs, Bitcoin scaling and Bitcoin-native finance developer. 'The venture firm Ribbit Capital led a seed funding round for Alpen in 2023' ($10.6M with Castle Island, Geometry, Stillmark, Robot Ventures and others; The Block, 2024-04-10). No later priced round found in the news sweep of 2026-09-28; Graduation left for the graduation pass. No source read places the company (The Block, its own site): city unknown, the country US from model knowledge. Momentum check: no round at or above $1B found.

Thermal battery maker, San Jose (Pulse 2.0; Crunchbase News). Ribbit is named among the new investors in the $550M Series C of July 2026, co-led by G2 Venture Partners and Eclipse (Pulse 2.0, 2026-08-02), its entry. The company did not disclose the valuation (Crunchbase News, 2026-07-30); a $550M round points to $1B or more but no figure exists, so the row carries needs_web_value for the web pass instead of a band.

Aside, Inc. is the company behind the charitable giving app Daffy: 'Aside, the company behind charitable giving app Daffy, has secured $17.1 million in Series A funding', led by Ribbit (Finovate, 2022-02-09; San Francisco), and daffy.org's footer reads 'Powered by Aside'. This row and the daffy row are one company (two listings on the firm's archived Our Bets page). Momentum check: no round at or above $1B found, news sweep 2026-09-28. Y Combinator's 'Aside' (a Fall 2025 agentic browser) is another company.

UK money-transfer app founded by Robinhood alumni. Amplo and Ribbit co-led the $4.5M seed (Tech Funding News, 2022-03-09). Deel acquired it for an undisclosed sum (Finovate, 2024-12-02: 'Deel has acquired U.K.-based international funds transfer company Atlantic Money'). No later round found before the sale; Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Online consumer lender, Chicago (the Series E release on General Atlantic's site). Ribbit's round is not on record: the $325M Series E of September 2015 names General Atlantic, Balyasny, J.P. Morgan, Tiger Global, August Capital, RRE and DFJ Growth, not Ribbit, and Ribbit's archive lists Avant from November 2015. Stage undetermined. The prefilled $1.98B comes from the unicorn snapshot (2015), not a cited priced round; left to the A/B pass.

axio, the Indian lending and BNPL company Capital Float, renamed axio in July 2022 (The Economic Times). Ribbit's first round was Capital Float's $45M Series C, 'led by Silicon Valley-based Ribbit Capital, with participation from existing investors SAIF Partners, Sequoia India and Creation Investments' (Indian Retailer, December 2017); Amazon continued the Series C with $22M in 2018 (KNN India). Amazon completed its roughly $200M cash acquisition in September 2025 (The Economic Times, 2025-09-04). Bengaluru, written Bangalore (Indian Retailer). This row and capital-float are one company. Accel's 'Axio' (a US company in Cambridge) is another company: name collision, not aligned.

Capital Float, the Indian lending and BNPL company Capital Float, renamed axio in July 2022 (The Economic Times). Ribbit's first round was Capital Float's $45M Series C, 'led by Silicon Valley-based Ribbit Capital, with participation from existing investors SAIF Partners, Sequoia India and Creation Investments' (Indian Retailer, December 2017); Amazon continued the Series C with $22M in 2018 (KNN India). Amazon completed its roughly $200M cash acquisition in September 2025 (The Economic Times, 2025-09-04). Bengaluru, written Bangalore (Indian Retailer). The acquisition closing is cited to https://m.economictimes.com/tech/funding/amazon-completes-200-million-cash-acquisition-of-axio-gets-nbfc-licence-in-india/articleshow/123695167.cms. This row and axio are one company (the firm linked capitalfloat.com 2017-2025 and lists axio.co.in today).

Ballet, crypto hardware wallets, founded by BTCC's Bobby Lee. It 'has raised an undisclosed amount of capital in a seed round backed by Ribbit Capital' and has 'a global headquarters in Las Vegas' (CoinDesk, 2019-09-12). No later priced round found in the news sweep of 2026-09-28; Graduation left for the graduation pass. The product is still sold and reviewed in 2025-2026 (99Bitcoins), so the status reads private.

Home batteries and power retail, Austin (TechCrunch). Ribbit's first round is the $1B Series C of October 2025, led by Addition with CapitalG, Elad Gil, Lightspeed, Ribbit, Thrive and Valor, at $3B pre-money (TechCrunch, 2025-10-08); the April 2025 $200M Series B names no Ribbit (TechCrunch). Ribbit then co-led the $1B Series D at $13B post-money with Addition, Valor and JPMorganChase (Pulse 2.0, 2026-08-03). Mark aligned with the a16z, Lightspeed and Spark rows.

Onchain transaction security, Tel Aviv (Fortune). Ribbit and Variant led the $27M Series A of October 2023 with Cyberstarts, Sequoia and Greylock (Calcalist, 2023-10-23); the earlier seed of about $6M is credited to Sequoia, Greylock and Cyberstarts on Greylock's row, not to Ribbit, so Ribbit entered at the Series A. Ribbit led the $50M Series B of February 2025 (Bloomberg). Momentum check: no round at or above $1B found, news sweep 2026-09-28. Aligned with the Greylock and Sequoia rows.

bonify (Forteil GmbH), consumer credit-score and personal finance app, Berlin. The EUR 5.5M Series A 'was led by London's Mosaic Ventures and Ribbit Capital, with participation from Index Ventures, DN Capital, HW Capital' (Tech.eu, 2017-02-21); EUR 5.5M @ ECB 2017-02-21 (EUR/USD 1.0537) = $5.8M. SCHUFA acquired Forteil in December 2022 for an undisclosed price (Tech.eu, 2022-12-21: 'Schufa absorbs German fintech Forteil'), and SCHUFA has run the bonify app since.

Borro, online lender against luxury assets, founded in London. Ribbit listed it on its 2012-2014 Bets pages, but no source read names Ribbit's round (deBanked names Victory Park, Canaan, Eden Ventures and Augmentum among its backers): stage undetermined. The business failed: Victory Park took it over through administration in November 2017 and it stopped new lending in 2019 (deBanked, 2019-10), then Luxury Asset Capital bought and relaunched Borro in February 2020 (Business Wire; Wikipedia). Insolvency followed by a sale reads acquired. City: London, the last headquarters of the company Ribbit backed; the relaunched US brand sits inside Luxury Asset Capital. Cited: https://debanked.com/2019/10/what-happened-to-borro/ and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borro.

Breezy, an AI operating system for residential real estate agents; 'The Los Angeles-based startup was founded in early 2024' (Pulse 2.0). Ribbit led the $10M pre-seed with Fifth Wall, DST Global Partners, Liquid 2 and others (Pulse 2.0, 2026-02-02); the source names the round pre-seed, so the stage is Pre-Seed and the row takes no S2A. Momentum check: no round at or above $1B found, news sweep 2026-09-28. Felicis's 'Breezy' (a 2017 seed, SaaS) is another company.

Bitcoin peer-to-peer lending platform (founders in Brazil and San Francisco, Finovate 2013). It 'received investments from Ribbit Capital, Foundation Capital, Pantera Capital' (Wikipedia) and Micky Malka named it among Ribbit's four bitcoin investments in March 2014 (CoinDesk). In November 2013 it was raising about $1M on AngelList (Finovate), but no source ties Ribbit to that or any named round: stage undetermined. It shut down entirely in 2017 (Wikipedia): defunct.

Campfire, AI-native ERP and accounting software (John Glasgow), headquartered in San Francisco (its Series A release). Ribbit co-led the $65M Series B of October 2025 with Accel as a new partner (the company's release, 2025-10-15); the $35M Series A of June 2025 was led by Accel and does not name Ribbit. Valuation undisclosed; momentum check: no round at or above $1B found, news sweep 2026-09-28. The prefilled Japan (JP) is a Wikidata namesake, disputed; aligned with the Accel and Y Combinator rows (San Francisco, US).

CAN Capital (Capital Access Networks), small-business financing since 1998. Ribbit listed it on its 2012-2018 pages, but no source read names Ribbit's round: stage undetermined. Operating and private in 2026: it bought an equipment-finance platform from Republic Bank, and its release says it is 'headquartered in Atlanta' (MonitorDaily, 2026-02-23, https://www.monitordaily.com/can-capital-acquires-equipment-finance-platform-from-republic-bank-finance-expanding-small-business-lending-capabilities/); Accel's row carries Kennesaw, the Atlanta-area office it moved its executive functions to in 2018 (deBanked, 2019). No valuation at or above $1B found.

Castle Technologies (castle.tech) turns business risks into tradeable event contracts on regulated venues; its site names Ribbit Capital and Jump Trading as its backers and shows it operating in August 2026 (https://castle.tech/). The prefilled acquired status comes from an SEC filer match on another Castle (cik_weak), disputed: private. No round naming Ribbit found in the news sweep (2026-09-28): stage undetermined; momentum check: no round at or above $1B found. No source read places the company (its site gives no address): city unknown, the country US from model knowledge. The First Round and Khosla rows named Castle (account-takeover security; property management) are other companies.

Chipper Cash, cross-border payments across Africa, San Francisco headquarters. Ribbit led the $30M Series B of November 2020 with Bezos Expeditions (Technext24, 2020-11-19); the $13.8M Series A of June 2020 was led by Deciens Capital and the report names no Ribbit (PC Tech Magazine). The FTX-led Series C extension of November 2021 valued it at about $2B (TechCabal). Collapse evidence rules the row below $1B: FTX marked its stake down to $1.25B in December 2022 (TechCrunch), and in 2023 the internal valuation was cut by 70% from $2.2B while sale talks with Zepz valued it at $250M to $500M (WeeTracker, 2023-08-17, https://weetracker.com/2023/08/17/chipper-valuation-cut-failed-sale/); no priced round since. For review: the evidence is a reported internal cut and a failed sale, not a priced round.

Cognition AI, maker of the Devin coding agent, headquartered in San Francisco (Wikipedia). Ribbit's first round is the over-$1B Series D at $26B of May 2026, where the company's own post welcomes 'new investors including Ribbit Capital, Atreides, and Layer Global' (cognition.com, 2026-05-27). Mark: the $2B Series E at $48B (TechCrunch, 2026-09-08), matching Bain Capital Ventures' row; the 8VC, General Catalyst, Khosla and Lux rows still carry the $10.2B of September 2025 (same band).

Cowboy Space Corporation (Aetherflux until May 2026), orbital data centers and launch, founded by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt; San Carlos (TechCrunch, 2025). Ribbit's round is not on record: the $50M Series A of April 2025 (Index and Interlagos, with Breakthrough, a16z and NEA) and the $275M Series B of May 2026 (Index, with Breakthrough, Construct, IVP and SAIC) do not name Ribbit (TechCrunch), so the stage is undetermined. Mark: the Series B at a $2B post-money valuation (TechCrunch, 2026-05-11), aligned with IVP's row; a16z's row still reads below $1B from before that round.

Deel, global payroll and HR, San Francisco. 'In October 2025, Deel raised a US $300 million Series E funding round co-led by Ribbit Capital and Andreessen Horowitz, bringing its valuation to approximately US $17.3 billion' (Wikipedia); Ribbit is not named in the Series A to D or the February 2025 secondary, and the firm's archived pages never listed Deel, so the Series E is its entry. The prefilled country 'Israel / United States' is a Wikidata string, not a country code, disputed: US. The $17.3B is re-sourced from the unicorn snapshot to the cited Series E. Deel also bought Atlantic Money, another Ribbit row, in 2024.

basis: Listed on the Rebels list (Jerry Ng, jago.com), but PT Bank Jago Tbk already traded on the Indonesia Stock Exchange as ARTO before Ribbit's entry (Tempo, 2021-01-26: ARTO closed at Rp6,825 on 25 January 2021). Ribbit's position was announced in October 2021 as a minority stake of undisclosed size in the listed bank ('Ribbit Capital recently bought a minority stake in a Jakarta-based digital bank Bank Jago', PYMNTS, https://www.pymnts.com/news/investment-tracker/2021/ribbit-capital-invests-in-indonesian-digital-bank-bank-jago/; under 5% by other reports), with no venture round. A purchase into an already-listed company with no venture entry is out (T3; decisions.md D4), as for Futu, Sea and Tinkoff.
